title: vLLM Continuous Batching Serving Gateway
subtitle: Roofline Inference Physics: Prefill (FLOPs) vs Decode (HBM) and Iteration-Level Scheduling
problem_statement: An AI inference cluster serving a 70B parameter LLM experiences severe GPU underutilization (18% compute utilization) and high P99 Time-To-First-Token (TTFT > 3.8s) under static batching. When requests with variable prompt lengths (100 tokens vs 8,000 tokens) are grouped together, shorter requests sit idle waiting for the longest request to finish generation.

faded_bug.description: Static batching holds completed sequence slots idle until the longest sequence finishes.

studio_1_runtime.correct_fix_diff:
- if any(not req.is_finished() for req in self.running_batch): return self.forward_decode()
+ # Dynamic continuous batching: evict finished sequences and inject new prefill prompts each step
+ self.running_batch = [r for r in self.running_batch if not r.is_finished()]
+ while len(self.running_batch) < self.max_batch_size and self.waiting_queue:
+     self.running_batch.append(self.waiting_queue.pop(0))

invariants.description: TTFT at P99 must remain under 250ms and Inter-Token Latency (ITL) under 25ms.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain the arithmetic intensity difference between the Prefill phase (GEMM, compute-bound) and the Decode phase (GEMV, memory-bandwidth bound).
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: If batch size is increased from 16 to 128, why does TTFT degrade while overall system token throughput (tokens/sec) increases?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: A user submits a 32,000 token prompt during peak traffic. How do chunked prefills prevent this request from starving in-flight decode streams?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: Cloud GPU instances cost $3.50/GPU-hour. How do you implement speculative decoding to achieve 2.5x speedup without accuracy degradation?

counter_probes.counter_question: A single 70B model in FP16 requires 140GB of VRAM. An 8x H100 node has 640GB. If memory bandwidth is saturated during decode, why does adding more nodes NOT improve single-stream latency?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: Decode phase is memory-bandwidth bound. Single-stream latency is constrained by memory clock speed, not raw FLOPS. Speculative decoding or FP8 KV-cache quantization is required to reduce memory traffic.
